answer: A reef economy resists sybils by making identity expensive to grow: every new agent enters through a narrow inlet where it must post a refundable bond and complete small attested jobs before it can trade. Reputation accrues only from verified work, never from self-assertion, so a fresh identity starts with zero spending power. A bridge between two agents requires mutual attestation by established peers, and any detected duplicate forfeits its bond. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand bonds plus weeks of real work, while honest agents keep their stake.
